answers.name: poc-studio
answers.purpose: Drop in a discovery-meeting transcript, brd or trd or any requriment doc for project and get, in under 5 minutes of agent time: requirements + action items, an AI architecture spec with costs, a running sector prototype, a GitHub repo with README and CI, a pitch deck, a prototype walkthrough video and docs.
answers.users: Just you (AI developer and full-stack developer at Skyform) running pre-sales PoCs. Clients only see what you share: the repo, the deck, the video and a read-only share page.
features: Dashboard: past runs with status, sector, client, cost per run and an hours-saved counter
New run: paste or drop a transcript (.txt, .vtt, .docx, .md), confirm sector and client name, options (deck style, repo visibility)
Meeting Intelligence: goals, ranked features, constraints, budget, timeline, sector, stakeholders, action items with owners (requirements.json)
Gate 1: brief shown as an editable form; approve to continue
Solution Architect: classifies the use case (RAG, agent, classifier, vision, forecasting), picks models, data flow, Mermaid diagram, monthly cost table (architecture.md)
Prototype Builder: picks one of 4 sector templates (healthcare, logistics, e-commerce, fintech), generates pages, forms, mock data and API stubs, runs npm build and fixes errors (max 3 loops)
Pitch & Docs (parallel with the build): 8-10 slide Reveal.js deck, executive summary, user flows; optional .pptx export
Prototype video: scripted Playwright walkthrough of the built prototype recorded to MP4/WebM, embedded in the deck
QA Reviewer: outputs agree (features, names, costs), build passed, no secrets, links work; failures go back to the owning agent at most twice
Gate 2: preview prototype (mobile/desktop toggle), deck and video; approve to publish
Repo & DevOps: create the GitHub repo on your account, README, .env.example, GitHub Actions CI, first push, issues from action items
Live run view: agent timeline over SSE with status, logs, tokens and cost per step
Request changes on any output: a note goes back to the owning agent, which revises only that artifact
Per-run token budget; the run pauses and asks when it is hit
non_goals: Login, teams, multi-tenant (single user on your machine; add auth only if it is ever shared)
Redis/Celery queue, S3, pgvector, E2B sandbox, Langfuse in v1 (local equivalents below; each is a later swap)
Audio transcription in v1 (transcripts arrive as text; local Whisper is a later add-on)
Auto-deploying client prototypes to production (Vercel preview is optional, on your yes)

stack.choice: Next.js 16 (App Router), Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Lucide, sileo toasts
stack.reason: Brief and proposal name Next.js; 16 is current (brief said 14). Generated prototypes use the same stack, so templates are shared.

stack.choice: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, Server-Sent Events
stack.reason: Proposal choice; SSE streams the agent timeline.

stack.choice: LangGraph supervisor, interrupt() at the 2 gates, SQLite checkpointer, runs as asyncio tasks in the API process
stack.reason: Proposal names LangGraph. No Redis/Celery: one user does not need a queue, and checkpoints already make runs resumable. $0.

stack.choice: SQLite (projects, runs, agent_steps, artifacts, approvals) + versioned files under ./runs/<id>/
stack.reason: Same 5-table model as the proposal; replaces Postgres + S3 at $0. Moves to Postgres with one URL change.

stack.choice: Skyform gateway (OpenAI-compatible): fast for extraction, smart for architecture and code, claude-haiku-5-5 only for deck polish
stack.reason: Brief budget rule: bulk work on the free Ollama models. Schema in the prompt, validated output, mock provider in tests.

stack.choice: Local Docker container per run (node:22, network limited to npm), plain folder fallback
stack.reason: Replaces E2B at $0; keeps generated code away from your secrets.

stack.choice: Reveal.js web deck + python-pptx export; Playwright headless recording for the prototype walkthrough
stack.reason: All free and local; the video is the new "video of that prototype" requirement.

stack.choice: Fine-grained personal token on Jegathpranava (repo create, contents, issues), via REST
stack.reason: Your own use; a GitHub App is overkill for one account. Generated client repos default to private.

stack.choice: Tokens, cost and duration per agent step in SQLite, shown on the run page
stack.reason: Covers the proposal KPI "cost per run" without Langfuse. Add Langfuse later if needed.

stack.choice: Local: one script starts web + API (docker compose optional)
stack.reason: Dev tier. The build loop runs npm builds and git pushes, which need a real machine. $0 hosting.

answers.notes:
Sources: docs/requirements/technical-solution-proposal.txt (PDF), problem-statement.txt (DOCX), owner-direction-2026-11-22.md.
Budget: target under $0.05 of paid LLM spend per run (only the Haiku deck polish is paid); everything else free or local.
KPIs from the proposal: full run under 5 minutes of agent time, 8 of 10 test transcripts produce a prototype that builds, cost per run tracked.
Build order (proposal phases, compressed): 1 core pipeline + Gate 1 + live view; 2 prototype builder with 4 sector templates; 3 deck, video, QA, Gate 2, GitHub publish; 4 request-changes, budget limits, PII redaction option.
Guardrails kept: nothing leaves the machine before Gate 2, secret scan blocks any push, generated repos private by default.
Existing .env stays git-ignored and untouched.
